item.title: [9] Josephson scanning tunneling spectroscopy in superconducting phases coexisting with pair-, charge-, and spin-density waves
item.description:
Last authors: Jasmin Bedow, Dirk K. Morr

Authors: Alyson Laskowski, Jasmin Bedow, Dirk K. Morr

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: STS theory for imaging intertwined density wave and superconducting orders in cuprates and TMDs.

Tags: #theory #STS #density-waves

Abstract: Here, the authors demonstrate that the recent observations in scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS) experiments of spatial oscillations in the energy position of the superconducting coherence peaks in the cuprate, transition metal dichalcogenide, iron-based, and heavy-fermion superconductors can arise from the possible presence of pair-, charge- or spin-density-wave phases. In all of these phases, the spatial oscillations of the superconducting order parameter can be imaged via the critical Josephson current, measured in Josephson STS experiments.

item.title: [8] Cooper-pair localization in the magnetic dynamics of a cuprate ladder
item.description:
Last authors: C. D. Batista, G. Alvarez, S. Johnston, and D. A. Tennant

Authors: A. Scheie, P. Laurell, J. Thomas, V. Sharma, A. I. Kolesnikov, G. E. Granroth, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Neutron scattering and DMRG study of localized Cooper pairs in a quasi-1D cuprate ladder.

Tags: #experiment #cuprate #neutron-scattering

Abstract: Localized Cooper pairs in a doped quantum ladder. Inelastic neutron scattering and DMRG calculations show that the magnetic dynamics of Sr 2 . 5 Ca 11 . 5 Cu 24 O 41 lack the incommensurate signatures expected from doped carriers. The results point to strongly localized hole pairs that preserve commensurate antiferromagnetic correlations, placing new constraints on the low-energy description of cuprate ladders and the mechanisms responsible for pairing in correlated quantum materials.

item.description:
Last authors: Spenser Talkington, Martin Claassen

Authors: Benjamin Kass, Spenser Talkington, Martin Claassen

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Methodological probe of magnetic phase boundaries, relevant to quantum magnet research.

Tags: #magnetism #method

Abstract: Cavity engineering holds promise for manipulating material properties, but measuring induced changes and attributing them to light-matter interactions remains challenging. Here, the authors show that polarization-dependent photon counting measurements of transmitted photons provide a symmetry-sensitive probe of many-body correlations in cavity-embedded systems. Additionally, deviations from Poissonian photon statistics reveal the magnitude of light-induced material changes. The authors demonstrate this approach for the Kitaev-Heisenberg family of two-dimensional magnets, identifying stripy and antiferromagnetic phases and their phase boundary.

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: author whitelist: Riccardo Comin

Tags: #ARPES #kagome #chargedensitywave #phonon

Abstract: The authors utilize phonon fluctuation diagnostics here to resolve the open question of the microscopic origin of charge density wave order in A V 3 Sb 5 ( A =K, Rb, Cs) kagome metals. Here, combining momentum-resolved a b i n i t i o calculations with ARPES measurements, they identify electron-phonon coupling as the primary driver of the lattice instability, rather than Van Hove singularities or nesting alone. Remarkably, the strongest contributions arise away from the high-symmetry M points, revealing a common mechanism across the three compounds.

item.title: [8] Microscopic magnetic phase evolution in the Weyl semimetal Mn3Sn revealed by μ+SR
item.description:
Last authors: Y. Sassa, M. Månsson

Authors: U. Miniotaite, O. K. Forslund, H. Luetkens, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Excellent experimental study of a relevant Weyl semimetal magnetic system.

Tags: #Weyl #material #magnetism

Abstract: The Weyl semimetal Mn 3 Sn hosts a rich sequence of magnetic states. Here, the authors combine muon spin relaxation and magnetization measurements to reveal a broad crossover between helical and inverse triangular antiferromagnetic order. At low temperatures, their nearly stoichiometric sample develops a growing ferromagnetic component and slowing spin fluctuations, without evidence of static spin-glass freezing within the experimental time window. These findings suggest that low-temperature ferromagnetism can emerge independently of glassy freezing.

item.title: [7] Magnetic diffuse scattering study of the dipolar-octupolar pyrochlore Ce2Sn2O7
item.description:
Last authors: J. Dudemaine, A. D. Bianchi, J. W. Kolis, and B. D. Gaulin

Authors: B. Yuan, M. Powell, X. Liu, J. Ni, E. M. Smith, R. Schäfer, R. Moessner, F. Ye, J. Dudemaine, A. D. Bianchi, J. W. Kolis, and B. D. Gaulin

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: High-quality neutron scattering study on quantum magnetic materials.

Tags: #neutronscattering #material #magnetism

Abstract: The Ce pyrochlores Ce 2 X 2 O 7 ( X = Sn, Hf, Zr) have attracted considerable attention as quantum spin ice candidates. So far, much of their physics has been interpreted by considering only nearest-neighbor interactions. Here, diffuse neutron scattering reveals that these interactions fail to explain the dominant spin correlations in Ce 2 Sn 2 O 7 even qualitatively. Instead, the observed correlations strikingly resemble those of classical dipolar spin ice, demonstrating a nonperturbative role of further-neighbor interactions in controlling its low-energy physics.
